thread:
amelia: FYI customer (acct: acme-inc) reporting bursts of 502s from hosted inference endpoint in eu-west-1 starting ~2026-03-15T03:18Z. They see TLS handshake timeouts in their client and curl; they say it started right after our cert rotation window. attaching their curl + dig outputs they sent.

ryan_infra: Can you paste the exact curl error they saw? also which customer AS/ISP?

amelia: Customer pasted: `curl -v https://inference.redwoodapi.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"` -> `* Connected to inference.redwoodapi.com (35.190.12.4) port 443 (#0)\n* TLS 1.3 connection (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)\n* TLS handshake timeout\n* Closing connection 0\ncurl: (56) Recv failure: Connection was reset`

amelia: Their dig: `;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345\n;; Query time: 240 msec\n;; SERVER: 192.0.2.53#53(192.0.2.53)`

ryan_infra: 240ms query time is high but not catastrophic. What stands out: connection to 35.190.12.4 (one of our edge IPs). Did they hit an old edge with expired/rotating cert?

dmitri_sre: Checking internal logs for that window now. infra-bot: please paste edge handshake error rates for eu-west between 03:10-03:30Z.

infra-bot: metric: edge.tls.handshake_timeout.count{region:eu-west} = +320 (03:12-03:22Z), baseline ~10. Top source prefixes: ASN 12345 (ISP-A), ASN 67890 (ISP-B).

dmitri_sre: That correlates with cert rotation at 03:20Z. We saw a short period where OCSP stapling warmup failed on a subset of edge nodes (staple fetch latency spiked), causing some clients (particularly older stacks and some ISP middleboxes) to abort handshakes.

ryan_infra: Also noting DNS resolver latency spikes from 192.0.2.53 in the same timeframe — possibly causing clients to retry and hit different edge IPs mid-rotation. combination of stale cached records + rotation -> hitting nodes missing stapled OCSP.

amelia: Customer says affected users are primarily on ISP-A and ISP-B in region. They can repro consistently when using their ISP resolver, but not when switching to 1.1.1.1.

dmitri_sre: Good repro vector. Ask them to run two quick checks and send outputs: (1) `dig +short inference.redwoodapi.com @their-resolver` (2) `curl -v --connect-timeout 10 https://inference.redwoodapi.com/v1/health` and paste full verbose.

ryan_infra: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) Have customer switch to a public resolver (1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8) as workaround. 2) On our side, we can temporarily increase LB handshake timeout from 5s -> 8s for eu-west to tolerate slow stapling. 3) Roll back across-edge stapling fetch concurrency to reduce cache misses during rotation.

dmitri_sre: Also recommend they test `curl --resolve` to force IP and skip DNS: `curl -v --resolve inference.redwoodapi.com:443:35.190.12.4 https://inference.redwoodapi.com/v1/generate` — if that works, DNS resolver path is implicated.

amelia: Customer ran `--resolve` and says the request completes (200) consistently. They collected an strace + tcpdump that shows RST after TLS ClientHello when using their ISP resolver.

ryan_infra: RST after ClientHello is consistent with middlebox/ISP aborting when it sees missing OCSP staple or unknown cert chain. We'll open an ops ticket to: (a) increase handshake timeout for eu-west, (b) temporarily expand cert overlap window for next rotation, (c) add a healthcheck to detect stapling miss rate and auto-roll back if >5% in 5m.

dmitri_sre: Creating internal incident: INC-20260315-01. Assigning to oncall to push the timeout bump and enable stapling fetch metrics alert.

support-bot: Incident INC-20260315-01 created by dmitri_sre. Priority: P2. Slack alert sent to #incidents.

ryan_infra: For customer-facing notes: explain that we saw a short cert/OCSP stapling warmup issue during rotation that, combined with some ISP resolver behavior, caused handshake aborts. Workarounds: switch resolver or use `--resolve` until we complete mitigation. We'll follow up once we have the LB timeout and metrics fix in place.

amelia: I'll pass that to the customer and request their packet capture + ISP ASN list. thanks everyone :pray:

dmitri_sre: One more repro command for them: `openssl s_client -connect inference.redwoodapi.com:443 -servername inference.redwoodapi.com -status -brief` — if status shows no OCSP response, collect that output.

amelia: customer asked ETA. dmitri_sre / ryan_infra any estimate on changes?

ryan_infra: Timeout bump is a simple LB config change, can be rolled in ~15-30m with canary. Stapling metrics alert + runbook in ~2h. Cert overlap policy change needs PM approval for next rotation window, but we can extend current overlap immediately by re-issuing with short TTL if necessary (engineering estimate 1-3h).

amelia: great. I'll update customer now and ask them to test public resolvers and share ASN + tcpdump.

support-bot: Note: please redact any API keys from packet captures before sharing.
